name: Aerial
works_with: Android TV 5.0 and later (Aerial Lite for 4.0 to 4.4), aimed at Xiaomi, TCL, Skyworth, Sony and other China-market TVs, boxes and projectors
short: A clean, ad-free home screen modelled on Apple TV for China-market Android TVs, with aerial screensavers and a full undo.
what: Aerial is an Android TV home screen with no ads and no recommendation feed: just your apps, a wallpaper and aerial-film screensavers. You can sort apps into folders, hide them, and rearrange them from your phone by scanning a QR code. On TVs that only accept their own home screen, it uses an accessibility service to switch back to Aerial whenever the stock home screen appears.
who: Owners of China-market TVs from Xiaomi, TCL, Skyworth, Sony, Hisense and others who are tired of the stock launcher's ads. The README has a supported-TVs table, so check your model there first. Some models can't be taken over yet.
needs: adb on a computer on the same network as the TV
ADB debugging turned on in the TV's settings (the README lists the steps per brand)

steps.title: Turn on ADB debugging
steps.text: On other Android TVs: Settings → Device Preferences → About → press Build 7 times, then turn on USB debugging in Developer options. Xiaomi, TCL, Haier and OPPO have their own steps in the README.

steps.title: Install with one command (macOS or Linux)
steps.text: `KEEP_ADB=1` turns ADB back on after Xiaomi switches it off in standby, so you can update later.

steps.title: Or install by hand
steps.text: Download `aerial-standard.apk` first. Run the last line about 5 seconds after Aerial shows: it makes Aerial smoother and takes some tens of seconds.
steps.code:
adb connect 192.168.1.20:5555
adb install -r aerial-standard.apk
adb shell pm grant app.orchard.tv android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
adb shell cmd notification allow_listener app.orchard.tv/app.orchard.tv.guard.RevivalListener
adb shell appops set app.orchard.tv SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow
adb shell am start -n app.orchard.tv/.MainActivity
adb shell cmd package compile -m speed -f app.orchard.tv

steps.title: If the TV refuses home-screen apps
steps.text: Add `-s guard` to the end of the one command, or use `aerial-guard.apk`.

steps.title: To undo it
steps.text: Add `--uninstall` to remove Aerial as well.

try.label: From the README
try.text: After installing, press Home. If Android asks which app to use, choose Aerial, then Always. If the old launcher comes back, open Aerial from the app list and follow Make Aerial Your Home Screen.

watch: The one-line install and undo pipe a script from aerial.qust.me straight into bash. Read the script before you run it.

The manual install grants `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS`, a notification listener and the overlay permission. On China-market TVs it also uses an accessibility service to keep itself as the home screen. The README says it only looks at which window is in front and reads no notifications.
The aerial films play from Apple's servers, the photo of the day comes from Bing, and the weather from Open-Meteo.
A boot ad comes from the TV's firmware and stays. Some models in the supported list only work with limits or can't be taken over.
